prohibited_concomitant: Silver dressings and dressings containing topical emollients (e.g. vaselinized gauze) as the standard-of-care dressing
On EB wound areas during the DBP: skin products such as creams (incl. barrier creams), ointments, gels, or emollients
On the EB target wound until confirmed closure/epithelialisation: silver dressings, silver sulfadiazine, topical antibiotics, topical steroids
Systemic steroids (except inhaled/ophthalmic/topical, e.g. budesonide for oesophageal strictures) until M3±14 days of open-label FU
Immunosuppressive therapy or cytotoxic chemotherapy until M3±14 days of open-label FU
Systemic antibiotics to treat EB target wound infections until M3±14 days of open-label FU
permitted_concomitant: Liquid antiseptics (polyhexanide, iodine products, octenidine dihydrochloride) at each dressing change to clean/reduce microbial colonisation prior to study treatment
Bathing (e.g. chlorhexidine, diluted bleach, or salt) prior to study treatment at each dressing change
Systemic antibiotics except for treatment of EB target wound infections
Inhaled, ophthalmic, or topical steroids (e.g. budesonide suspension for oesophageal strictures)
On non-target single EB wounds: silver sulfadiazine, topical antibiotics, topical steroids
value.population_note: Both arms (Oleogel-S10 and vehicle) receive study medication applied topically to EB partial-thickness wounds, then covered with a standard-of-care non-adhesive wound dressing (Section 6.3); SOC dressings are not fully standardized across sites/patients but silver dressings and emollient-containing dressings are excluded. Section 7.5.1/7.5.2 give detailed permitted/non-permitted concomitant medication lists.

method_citations: Cui, Hung, Wang (CHW) weighted test-statistic for sample size re-estimation

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: 7.6 Level of Significance, Multiple Comparisons and Multiplicity: The overall level of significance for the primary endpoint analysis is 0.05 (two-sided). At the final analysis, the primary endpoint is tested at the 5% significance level. If the primary analysis is statistically significant, the confirmatory testing approach continues hierarchically with statistical testing of the key secondary endpoints at the 5% significance level (see Section 9.3 for more details). The Cui, Hung, Wang (CHW) weighted test-statistic for sample size re-estimation does not require an adjustment of the significance level as the IA is for sample size re-estimation only and does not allow for early stopping due to early efficacy. All further analyses are considered as non-confirmatory and descriptive only.

value.source_inconsistency: The protocol/SAP express all timing in study DAYS, not weeks: primary efficacy endpoint at D45±7 (~week 6.4), End of Double-Blind Phase (EDBP) at D90±7 (~week 12.9, rounded here to week 13), then an open-label follow-up phase to M3/M12/M24 (~24 months, rounded here to week 117 total). primary_endpoint_week is left null rather than force a rounded value since the schema's week-granularity does not cleanly represent a D45 endpoint; see visit_days for the exact day-based schedule.

systemic_agents: Systemic antibiotics for target wound infection
value.rationale: No formal rescue-medication protocol for treatment failure (non-healing wound) is described; patients simply continue on randomized study medication/vehicle through the DBP regardless of wound healing progress. The only medication explicitly permitted specifically to address a clinical event (wound infection) is systemic antibiotics for target-wound infection, which is treated as concomitant medication, not a rescue provision changing study-drug status. Administration of non-permitted concomitant medication is instead listed as a criterion for withdrawal/discontinuation.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: 7.5.1 Permitted Concomitant Medication: ... Systemic antibiotics except for treatment of EB target wound (and other wounds matching target wound criteria) infections [is listed under non-permitted, i.e. antibiotics FOR target-wound infection are the one systemic-antibiotic exception permitted]. ... Administration of non-permitted concomitant medication(s) [is a withdrawal/discontinuation criterion].
